entities.summary:
Hezbollah is a Shia Islamist political party and armed organization headquartered in Beirut, Lebanon, founded in 1982 by Imad Mughniyah. The group's origins are deeply rooted in the Iranian-backed resistance to Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon, drawing on the legacy of the 1978 Islamic Resistance Movement (IRM) and its charismatic leader Musa al-Sadr.

 Heavily influenced by the 1983 Beirut barracks bombing, which killed 299 US Marines, Hezbollah's primary objective is to liberate Palestine from Israeli control. The group has been a key player in Lebanese politics, participating in multiple governments and contributing to regional instability through its military actions, including the 2006 Lebanon War.

 Despite facing economic sanctions and designation as a terrorist organization by several countries, Hezbollah maintains strong ties with Iran and has managed to adapt to the changing global landscape, leveraging its influence within the Arab world and beyond. Its military capabilities and social services have allowed it to maintain a broad base of support among Lebanese civilians.

 Hezbollah's legacy is complex, marked by both nationalist fervor and regional instability. As a major player in modern Middle Eastern politics, its impact will continue to be felt for years to come.

 'The only way to win the battle of wits against Israel is to develop an atomic bomb,' - Hassan Nasrallah, Hezbollah leader since 1992.
